title: Choose Job Scraper's visual world
question: The roll assigned Find-in-Files. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Find-in-Files
options.lineage: a code editor's search panel (grep results)
options.thesis: Your resume is the query: skills sit in the search bar as tokens, and each job is a result whose matched lines are highlighted like hits.
options.viewport: A query bar of skill tokens across the top with a live '72 results in 766 postings' readout. Below, results grouped by job: title, company and location, then 1–3 excerpt lines with your skills highlighted, the match count in the gutter. A status bar at the bottom shows boards, last fetch and your account.
options.risk: If it slides into dark-mode-plus-neon it becomes every developer tool; it has to stay a bright, paper-white editor.

raised.raise: Live readout: toggling a skill token re-ranks the list instantly, and the results count updates in place like an axis readout.
Rank is shown by how much detail a result gets: top matches show their highlighted excerpt lines, lower matches collapse to one line.
Switched-off skills and disabled users print in grayscale rather than disappearing.

options.label: Long Brown Envelope
options.thesis: Your profile is the long brown envelope: resume, 2x2 photo, clearances. Jobs are what you slip it toward.
options.viewport: Your envelope on the left with its contents (resume, skills) peeking out; the matched jobs stacked to the right as stamped slips.
options.risk: Instantly recognisable to Filipinos, but the kraft-paper warmth sits close to the overused cream-paper look and can feel nostalgic, not current.

options.label: Timetable Rack
options.thesis: One type size everywhere; rank carried by weight, case and reversed plates.
options.viewport: Jobs as timetable rows in strict columns (role, company, region, posted, match), the best match reversed into a solid plate.
options.case: Very scannable for a long list, but job seekers don't see themselves in an airline timetable.
options.risk: Goldenrod everywhere is tiring for a daily tool.

options.label: High-Density Portal
options.thesis: Pack far more jobs per screen in boxed, hairline-ruled modules with small red tabs.
options.viewport: A tiled wall of compact job modules with NEW and PH-OK badges, filters as a tab rail.
options.case: Matches the dense job portals PH users already know; loses on showing why each job matched.
options.risk: Tiny type hurts on phones and for tired eyes.

options.label: Type Specimen
options.thesis: Drag an axis, the whole page remaps live.
options.case: Nothing to do with job hunting.
options.kept: Every control change re-ranks live with a visible readout.

options.label: Character Goods Catalog
options.thesis: A ranked pastel grid with name plates.
options.case: Too playful for a job search.

options.label: Lexicon Plate
options.thesis: Entries ranked by how much apparatus each gets.
options.viewport: A dense text column with guide words.
options.case: Reads as a book, not a tool.

options.label: Midnight Transit Map
options.thesis: Routes and interchanges on midnight blue.
options.viewport: Skills as lines, jobs as stations.
options.kept: A clear state vocabulary: new, open, closed.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean job board (LinkedIn Jobs / Indeed class), done impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Search and location bar on top, filters on the left, job cards in the centre.
canonCard.risk: Looks like every other job board by design.
